Subject: INTERNAL: Proposed response to Nimbus — objection window and DPA redline

Team — internal note (please keep offline until we send):

Summary of position: we can accept a 45-day objection period for subprocessors tied to EEA processing as long as we:
- Limit scope to subprocessors that will 'process' EEA customer data (not all vendor categories).
- Provide a monthly cadence of consolidated notifications rather than per-change emails if they prefer fewer notices.
- Preserve the standard fallback: if objective material breach risk is raised and unresolved in the window, Redwood will either agree mitigation or suspend the new subprocessor for that customer.

DPA redline highlights (DPA_redline_v3.docx):
- Export-control carveout: we added specific language that the screening is limited to legal compliance checks (export control, OFAC, sanctions) and will not be used to mass-restrict lawful EEA processing.
- Transfer mechanism: we reference SCCs for EU transfers and include an Appendix listing EU-hosted subprocessors.

Action items for Rishi/Logan:
- Rishi: confirm commercial okay with 45 days or propose the monthly notification compromise.
- Logan: prepare DocuSign envelope with signers: 1) Redwood VP Legal (Neha Kapoor) — sign first; 2) Redwood Sales Ops (Rishi) — internal approval; 3) Nimbus Legal/Procurement — final signature. Use the DocuSign template 'DPA_Simple_Sign' and set reminder at +4 days.
